question: What does the term pharmacokinetics primarily describe?

options.A: How diseases spread in a community
options.B: What a drug does to the body
options.C: What the body does to a drug
options.D: How herbs interact with modern drugs

explanation: Pharmacokinetics focuses on how the body handles a medication through absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T4#BMP124_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which set of letters correctly represents the four main stages of pharmacokinetics?
explanation: The stages stand for Absorption, Distribution, Metabolism, and Excretion. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T4#BMP124_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which administration route completely bypasses the absorption phase?
explanation: Giving a drug straight into a vein puts it directly into the circulation, meaning no absorption step is needed. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T4#BMP124_U1_T4_h2)

question: Why is oral drug absorption often delayed during pregnancy?

options.A: Gastric acid production drops to zero
options.D: Blood flow to the stomach increases

explanation: High progesterone levels during pregnancy relax smooth muscle, slowing down gut movement and delaying how fast drugs enter the blood. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T4#BMP124_U1_T4_h2)

question: What type of drug molecule can cross biological membranes and have an effect?
explanation: Only drugs that are not attached to plasma proteins are small and active enough to slip across membranes to target sites. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T4#BMP124_U1_T4_h3)

question: A pregnant patient receives a water-soluble antibiotic. How might the large increase in her body water affect the drug?

options.A: It will stay entirely in her fat tissues
options.B: It may require higher doses to reach effective levels
options.C: It will turn into a solid crystal in the blood
options.D: It will fail to cross the placenta completely

explanation: More body fluid dilutes water-soluble medicines, meaning standard doses might be too weak to work effectively. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T4#BMP124_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which organ is primarily responsible for metabolizing most drugs in the body?
explanation: The liver contains specialized enzyme systems that break down and alter drug molecules. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T4#BMP124_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of drug metabolism?

options.B: To turn drugs into water-soluble forms for easy removal
options.C: To make every drug stick permanently to fat tissues
options.D: To stop the stomach from absorbing food

explanation: Metabolism changes fat-loving drug molecules into water-friendly waste products that the kidneys can filter out. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T4#BMP124_U1_T4_h4)

question: Which organ serves as the primary site for drug excretion?
explanation: The kidneys filter blood and pass water-soluble drug waste out through the urine. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T4#BMP124_U1_T4_h5)

question: How does normal pregnancy affect the clearance of drugs that leave the body through the kidneys?

options.A: Clearance stays exactly the same as in non-pregnant women
options.B: Clearance is faster because kidney filtration increases
options.C: Clearance stops completely until after childbirth
options.D: Clearance is slower due to blocked ureters

explanation: Pregnant women have a higher glomerular filtration rate, meaning kidney-cleared drugs leave the system quicker. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T4#BMP124_U1_T4_h5)

question: A midwife notes that a pregnant patient needs an increased dose of a renally cleared drug to maintain therapeutic levels. What physiological change best explains this?
explanation: Faster kidney filtration pushes the drug out of the blood quicker, often necessitating higher or more frequent doses. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T4#BMP124_U1_T4_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical pharmacokinetic change seen during pregnancy?
explanation: Total body water actually increases substantially during pregnancy, rather than decreasing. [learn more](BMP124_U1_T4#BMP124_U1_T4_h6)
